title: pre-weekend-mode-ops-quiet-qa-scratch
content:
Purpose:
This is a scratchpad for a short, low-friction comms push about 'weekend mode' (light staffing + stricter throttles) we plan to run before the long weekend. Intention is to reassure product teams and customers while making sure oncall and SRE have aligned expectations.

Audience:
- Internal: all engineers + product (primary), customer-support escalation path, growth for billing ops notice.
- External: only customers on Dedicated with active incidents (via normal incident comms) — we are NOT doing a wide customer email for this change.

Channels & Timing (draft):
- Thursday 18:00 PT: short Slack post in #all-hands-summary + #eng to set context (1–2 lines + link to FAQ).
- Thursday 18:05 PT: pinned micro-FAQ in #oncall-ops for oncall/readthrough.
- Friday 09:00 PT: optional 8-minute drop-in Q&A (calendar invite) for leads who want to ask specifics.

One-line Slack blurb (candidate):
"Heads-up: we'll be in 'Weekend Mode' from 2026-03-20 22:00 PT through 2026-03-23 08:00 PT. Reduced response targets; automatic throttles and stricter retries will be in effect for non-critical workloads. If you own a critical flow, add yourself to the weekend-sre rota or reply here now. Full FAQ -> <link>"

Why we need this (notes for leadership):
- Reduce operational noise for predictable non-business hours (lower headcount, global holiday overlap).
- Prevent noisy automated retries from consuming burst capacity and hurting latency for critical routes.
- Give SRE predictable constraints to tune autoscaling/cost controls.

Key backing behaviors (what platform will do):
- Enforce stricter burst limits for hosted API consumer keys with >99th percentile token rate patterns.
- Enable preference for grace degradation (route traffic to smaller quantized variants) instead of hard fail for some tiers.
- Slightly lower autoscaler floor for non-dedicated pools to avoid noisy spin-ups.

What to tell product/feature owners (bullet notes):
- If your feature must remain at normal latency, mark it as critical in the weekend gating form (link) and provide a contact.
- Consider batched/async fallbacks for non-interactive flows where possible.
- Expect TOI (time-of-impact) metrics in the Console dashboard after weekend.

Anticipated questions + draft answers (QA):
Q: Will customer SLAs be impacted?
A: For Hosted API normal SLA windows remain; however operational response times will be longer for non-critical incidents during weekend mode. Dedicated customers with contracts are handled per their SLA. We will not intentionally degrade SLA-backed endpoints.

Q: What do you mean by 'automatic throttles'?
A: Temporary soft-limit reductions applied to high-sustained session rates to prevent noisy retries from consuming the pool. These are reversible and logged.

Q: How do we exclude a route from throttles?
A: Use the 'critical' tag in route config and fill the weekend exemption form (link). SRE will review during the Friday morning check-in.

Q: I'm oncall — what's my expectation?
A: Primary oncall remains responsible for P1s. For P2/P3 we may queue and patch in the morning depending on impact. If you're the owner of a critical flow, please add yourself to the weekend rota or coordinate with your lead.

Q: Will hosted customers see heavier latencies?
A: Non-critical and exploratory workloads may see slightly higher 95th/99th percentiles due to stricter batch/coalescing behavior. Critical user-facing traffic will be prioritized.

Operational checklist (short):
- [ ] Pin weekend FAQ in #oncall-ops (Ravi)
- [ ] Publish allowed exemptions spreadsheet and form (Lina)
- [ ] Validate autoscaler floor toggles in staging (Maya)
- [ ] Smoke-check fallback routing in canary region (Adrian)
- [ ] Confirm paging thresholds and escalation matrix (oncall runbook) (Ravi)
- [ ] Prepare rollback notes and one-click scripts for throttles (SRE-tooling)

Open questions / blockers (personal notes):
- Need a clear label for 'non-interactive batch' vs 'low-latency interactive' in the Console; do we already have this taxonomy? if not, file small UX task.
- Quick metric we can expose in the Slack post to prove 'we're monitoring' — maybe a live token-rate gauge embed? (ask frontend)
- Legal/CS: confirm we can message this in the public #customer-updates if a large outage occurs; otherwise keep internal.

Suggested micro-FAQ (for pin):
Q: Who authorizes exemptions?
A: SRE lead + product owner sign-off. Use the exemptions form and add justification.

Q: Who do I ping for urgent pager fires?
A: Primary oncall as usual, then SRE escalations. Use @oncall in slack; don't DM multiple people.

Draft short email for leaders (if needed):
Subject: Weekend-mode notice + expected behaviors
Body: Hi all — we are enabling a temporary 'weekend mode' for the upcoming long weekend to reduce noisy retries and keep critical flows healthy. If you rely on low-latency behavior for customer-facing features, mark your routes as critical by EOD Thursday. We will run limited autoscaling and temporary throttles; detailed FAQ is pinned in #oncall-ops.

Fallback plan / rollback (short):
- Revert throttle config via config-service (1-click rollback script).
- Reenable normal autoscaler floor.
- Re-run canary traffic for 30 minutes to validate.

Notes-to-self for Friday run-through:
- Walk through the pin in #oncall-ops with Ravi at 09:00.
- Confirm Maya has approval from product leadership for exemptions timeline.
- Prepare a 3-slide pause-deck in case execs ask for quick status (1: why, 2: impact summary, 3: rollback readiness).

Finish: this doc is a working scratchpad — will convert to a short Slack and pinned FAQ once checklist items are green. Keep edits minimal and time-box to Thursday EOD.
